blocks.text: OS X Yosemite 10.10 reached the Mac App Store on October 16, 2014. The major release combined a broad visual redesign with Continuity, cloud-file, search, notification, browser, mail, messaging, media, family-account, developer-platform, compatibility, and security changes.

blocks.text: Apple announced Yosemite on June 2 and made a developer preview available that day. It also announced a customer beta program for later in the summer. The retained launch announcement then confirms October 16 as the public availability date; this article attaches editorial content only to that durable public route.

citations.locator: June 2, 2014; developer preview and beta-program timing

blocks.text: The release revised core interface materials and typography while adding several ways for compatible Macs and iOS devices to cooperate: activity handoff, easier hotspot access, cross-platform AirDrop, carrier-message relay, and iPhone calling.

Yosemite added Today widgets, broader Spotlight results, Finder-based iCloud Drive, new Safari and Mail workflows, richer Messages controls, iTunes 12, and Family Sharing. Apple also tied the release to Swift and expanded SpriteKit and SceneKit tooling.

blocks.text: The structured public-release changes below require confirmation in Apple's October launch material or its version-specific 10.10 advisory. June-only preview details are not promoted into public deltas, later 10.10.x fixes are not projected backward, comparative Safari statements remain attributed to Apple, and no build number or undocumented behavior is inferred.

events.summary: OS X Yosemite 10.10 reached the public channel on October 16, 2014 with a redesigned Mac experience, new cross-device workflows, expanded apps and services, developer technologies, broad compatibility, and a documented security baseline.

blocks.text: Apple made Yosemite available on October 16, 2014 as a free download from the Mac App Store. Apple's archived 2014 security index independently places OS X Yosemite v10.10 on the same date and lists Mac OS X 10.6.8 or later as the upgrade audience.

The release entries synthesize the confirmed launch package across system design, Continuity, Notification Center, Spotlight, iCloud Drive, Safari, Mail, Messages, iTunes, Family Sharing, developer frameworks, installation compatibility, and the initial Yosemite security advisory.

citations.locator: Launch overview through developer platform paragraph
OS X Yosemite v10.10 security content

blocks.text: Apple described a broad Mac hardware baseline but imposed narrower requirements on some Continuity features. Those features depended on iOS 8.1 and, in some cases, newer Bluetooth LE and Wi-Fi capabilities; hotspot and calling also remained subject to carrier service and possible cellular charges.

This event is the initial 10.10 public release only. Apple's 2014 index separately lists 10.10.1 on November 17, but the local catalog has no corresponding durable version route, so that point release and its fixes are excluded rather than folded into Yosemite 10.10.

changes.title: Redesigned system appearance
changes.canonicalSummary: Yosemite refreshed the Mac interface with streamlined toolbars, translucency, redesigned icons, and a new system typeface.
changes.summary: The public release reworked core visual surfaces while retaining familiar Mac interaction patterns, giving content more room and using translucent sidebars and controls to convey context.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Handoff between Mac and iOS devices
changes.canonicalSummary: Handoff let supported Mac and iOS apps transfer an in-progress activity from one nearby device to another.
changes.summary: A user could begin work such as composing mail or browsing the web on one supported device and continue the same activity on another, subject to Apple's Continuity requirements.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Instant Hotspot
changes.canonicalSummary: Instant Hotspot simplified connecting a Mac to a nearby iPhone's personal hotspot.
changes.summary: Yosemite exposed an eligible iPhone hotspot through the Mac's network workflow without a separate manual setup sequence; carrier availability still applied.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: AirDrop between Mac and iOS
changes.canonicalSummary: AirDrop expanded to exchange content directly between supported Macs and iOS devices.
changes.summary: The release removed the earlier same-platform boundary from Apple's nearby file-sharing workflow, allowing compatible Mac and iOS devices to send content to one another.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: SMS and MMS relay on Mac
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages on Mac could display and send SMS and MMS traffic relayed through a nearby iPhone.
changes.summary: Yosemite extended the Mac messaging experience beyond iMessage by using a compatible iPhone to relay carrier text and multimedia messages across a user's devices.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: iPhone calls on Mac
changes.canonicalSummary: A Mac could place and receive cellular calls through a nearby compatible iPhone.
changes.summary: The Continuity calling path let the Mac act as a speakerphone for the user's iPhone, with Apple's cellular-charge and device-capability qualifications still in force.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Notification Center Today view and widgets
changes.canonicalSummary: Notification Center gained a Today view with Apple information panels and support for downloadable widgets.
changes.summary: The new view collected timely information such as calendars, weather, stocks, reminders, clocks, and social activity, and it could be extended with compatible Mac App Store widgets.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Spotlight rich results
changes.canonicalSummary: Spotlight moved to a prominent desktop search interface and added results from Apple services, maps, reference material, the web, news, and showtimes.
changes.summary: Yosemite broadened Spotlight from local search into a combined discovery surface that could return contextual information from several online and on-device categories.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: iCloud Drive in Finder
changes.canonicalSummary: iCloud Drive exposed cloud files as a Finder location with folders, tags, search, and access from supported Apple devices and Windows PCs.
changes.summary: The release gave users a general-purpose file hierarchy for organizing arbitrary document types in iCloud and reaching them across supported platforms.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Streamlined Safari with efficiency improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari adopted a simplified interface, while Apple reported faster browsing performance and longer Mac battery life for web and Netflix HD video.
changes.summary: The Yosemite launch positioned Safari around a content-first layout and efficiency gains. The performance and battery statements are Apple's launch claims rather than independent benchmark findings.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Markup in Mail
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail added tools for annotating images and completing or signing forms and PDFs without leaving a message.
changes.summary: The composer gained an integrated attachment-editing workflow for common review, annotation, form-completion, and signature tasks.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Mail Drop for large attachments
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail Drop provided an Apple-hosted delivery path for attachments as large as 5 GB.
changes.summary: Yosemite let Mail users send files that would commonly exceed email attachment limits, with the launch material setting a maximum size of 5 GB.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Expanded Messages conversation controls
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages added controls for group membership, shared locations, conversation attachments, and notification muting.
changes.summary: The public release made group threads easier to manage by allowing participant changes, location viewing, quick attachment access, and per-conversation notification suppression.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: iTunes 12 redesign and Recents
changes.canonicalSummary: iTunes 12 introduced a new interface, simpler library-to-store navigation, and a Recents view for recently acquired or played media.
changes.summary: The bundled media app was reorganized to reduce friction between a user's collection and store discovery while surfacing recent activity in one place.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Family Sharing purchases
changes.canonicalSummary: Family Sharing let participating family members browse and download one another's eligible Apple media and Mac App Store purchases.
changes.summary: Yosemite brought the shared-purchase side of Apple's family account model to the Mac across supported iTunes, iBooks, and Mac App Store content.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Swift development language
changes.canonicalSummary: Yosemite's developer platform included Apple's new Swift programming language for building OS X and iOS software.
changes.summary: Apple presented Swift as a modern language integrated into its application-development stack, with goals that included interactivity, reliability, and safer implementation.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Expanded SpriteKit and SceneKit game tools
changes.canonicalSummary: SpriteKit gained richer motion, lighting, and physics workflows and could be combined with SceneKit for animated 3D scenes.
changes.summary: The Yosemite developer stack expanded Apple's first-party frameworks for constructing two-dimensional game behavior and integrating it with three-dimensional scene content.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Free Mac App Store upgrade and hardware baseline
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple distributed Yosemite as a free Mac App Store upgrade for Macs from 2009 onward and selected 2007 and 2008 models.
changes.summary: The broad installation baseline remained wider than the eligibility for every Continuity capability; Apple separately noted that some cross-device features required newer Bluetooth LE and Wi-Fi hardware and iOS 8.1.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Network credential and transport repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: Yosemite's security baseline addressed Wi-Fi credential exposure, AFP address disclosure, Bluetooth pairing, certificate policy, and SSL 3.0 transport risks.
changes.summary: Apple's advisory records hardening across enterprise Wi-Fi authentication, file sharing, Bluetooth input connections, certificate trust, and Secure Transport, including its response to the SSL 3.0 CBC weakness.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

citations.locator: 802.1X; AFP File Server; Bluetooth; Certificate Trust Policy; Secure Transport

changes.title: Access control, session, and code-signing repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: The release tightened app sandbox access, screen-lock behavior, encrypted-volume state, account sessions, configuration profiles, and application signature validation.
changes.summary: The version-specific advisory documents authorization, state-management, persistence, and signature-validation corrections spanning the sandbox, Dock, storage encryption, Lost Mode, login, profiles, SecurityAgent, and code signing.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Kernel, driver, and filesystem repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: Yosemite repaired memory-safety, validation, disclosure, privilege, and denial-of-service vulnerabilities in drivers, IOKit, filesystems, and the kernel.
changes.summary: Apple's advisory covers graphics and input drivers, IOKit data queues, HFS handling, Mach ports, IPv6 processing, system-control sockets, and early-boot hardening randomness.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.

changes.title: Application and bundled-library repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: The initial Yosemite security release updated server components and repaired issues in Mail, file sharing, QuickTime, Safari, and related system services.
changes.summary: Apple documented Apache and Bash updates plus corrections for unintended mail recipients, file-sharing state, malicious audio processing, Safari history and push behavior, and ASN.1 parsing. The advisory also states that Safari 8 incorporated Safari 7.1 security content.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated public-launch announcement or version-specific security advisory to the existing audited Yosemite 10.10 public-release event.
